fields.expected:
The project that maps most directly onto developer-productivity work at Bear Robotics is a job-application agent I built in TypeScript and Node. The problem was ordinary repetitive browser work: opening ATS pages, refilling the same fields, tracking state. What made it interesting was that a fully autonomous browser agent is dangerous here, since one wrong action submits a real application or fabricates an answer. So I designed it as a deterministic, operator-controlled agent. Every application moves through an explicit state machine from DISCOVERED through SUBMITTED, SQLite is the single source of truth because state diverging across processes is how automation quietly breaks, and every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED that never default on. I also built a validation ladder from UNIT_CONFIRMED to LIVE_MUTATION_CONFIRMED, because a capability passing against a local fixture does not mean it works against reality. Free-text and demographic fields always escalate to human review.

I have also built and shipped things people use: an iOS health product in a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users, and an ML anomaly-detection service with a versioned FastAPI microservice and CI scaffold I own. I would want to work on the internal tooling and AI agents, and on making them trustworthy enough that engineers actually turn them on.
